title: Full health checkup
what: A set of tests, scans, and doctor visits in one or a few visits. It helps find problems before they cause symptoms.
why: For prevention, usually once a year. The program is chosen by your age, sex, and family history.
duration: usually 2 to 4 hours, sometimes over several days
tell_doctor: What bothers you, even small things
What medicines and supplements you take
Diseases in your parents, brothers, and sisters

prepare.title: Fasting
prepare.text: Usually no food for 8 to 12 hours before blood tests. Plain still water is fine.

prepare.title: The day before
prepare.text: Eat a light dinner. No alcohol for 1 to 2 days. No hard workouts or sauna.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop them on your own. Ask the clinic whether to take your morning medicines before or after the blood test.

prepare.title: Urine test
prepare.text: Collect your first morning urine in a sterile container from the pharmacy.

prepare.title: For women
prepare.text: If you will have swabs taken, it is best not during your period. Check with the clinic.

bring: The container with your morning urine
A snack and water, to eat after the blood test
steps: In the morning, before eating, your blood is taken
Then tests that need an empty stomach, like a belly ultrasound
After that, you can have a snack
Next, an ECG and other tests in your program
At the end, a doctor goes over the results and gives advice
feel: A quick prick for the blood test
Nothing else is usually unpleasant, but the day can be tiring
after: Some results are ready the same day, others in a few days
If something is found, your doctor will tell you what to do next
Keep your results. They are useful for comparing next year

faq.q: How often should I have a checkup?
faq.a: Usually once a year. If you have a long-term illness, your doctor may set a different schedule.

faq.q: Can I drink water before the tests?
faq.a: Yes, plain still water is fine. No tea, coffee, juice, or chewing gum.

faq.q: Why have a checkup if nothing hurts?
faq.a: Many diseases have no signs for a long time: high blood pressure, high sugar, high cholesterol. A checkup finds them early, when treatment is easier.

reminders.text: Checkup the morning after tomorrow. From today, no alcohol and no hard workouts.
Checkup tomorrow. After a light dinner, do not eat. Still water is fine. Get your urine container ready.
